samples.originalTitle: DeMar DeRozan Receiving Interest From Heat, Nuggets, Cavaliers
samples.originalSummary: DeMar DeRozan is currently the most significant free agent available on the market and he's drawing interest from the Miami Heat, Denver Nuggets and Cleveland Cavaliers. " I'm told Miami, Denver, and Cleveland are among the teams interested in Demar DeRozan," said Shams Charania on Monday's episode of NBA Today. The Heat and Cavaliers were among the finalists for LeBron James before he signed with the Philadelphia 76ers. DeRozan had a partial guarantee on his contract for only $10 million of the total of $26.74 million with the Sacramento Kings. DeRozan, who is represented by Aaron Goodwin , appeared in 77 games last season with the Kings and averaged 18.4 points, 2.9 rebounds and 4.1 assist. DeRozan will be playing in his age-37 season.

samples.originalTitle: Heat Waiting On Klay Thompson Before Filling Out Roster
samples.originalSummary: The Miami Heat have a handful of roster spots to fill before the regular season. They've been linked to several veteran wing shooters and scorers, with one particular target in mind. The Heat are focused on adding Klay Thompson, even if it's unclear if the veteran wing will part ways with the Dallas Mavericks. Thompson is owed $17.5 million in the final year of his contract with the Mavs. It's unknown if the player or team has interest in a buyout. Dallas is facing a bit of a roster crunch with 16 players on standard contracts for just 15 roster spots. While Miami is willing to wait on Thompson, they are keeping tabs with other veterans. That group includes DeMar DeRozan, who was waived by the Sacramento Kings earlier this offseason, as well as Bradley Beal, who declined a player option with the LA Clippers to open the offseason. The Heat are also in the market for another big man. There isn't a pure center on the roster, with Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bam Adebayo and Bobby Portis the top three bigs in the Miami rotation.

samples.originalTitle: Wizards, Mavericks Had No Interest In Trading Anthony Davis, Kyrie Irving
samples.originalSummary: There had been reporting that LeBron James was interesting in teaming up with one of his former teammates when he picked a new team. The Golden State Warriors and Cleveland Cavaliers were linked to Anthony Davis and Kyrie Irving, respectively. However, neither Davis' current team, the Washington Wizards, nor Irving's current team, the Dallas Mavericks, had any interest in trading either player. In addition, James, nor his agent Rich Paul of Klutch Sports, made no demands of teams that they must trade for Davis or Irving to get the NBA's all-time leading scorer. Ultimately, James picked the Philadelphia 76ers for the upcoming season. It's expected that both Davis and Irving will start the season with the Wizards and Mavericks, respectively.

samples.originalTitle: Nuggets Matching Spencer Jones Offer Sheet From Thunder
samples.originalSummary: The Denver Nuggets are matching the two-year, $12 million offer sheet Spencer Jones signed with the Oklahoma City Thunder. Denver will retain Jones, who became a valuable rotation player for them last season. Matching the offer sheet for Jones will push the Nuggets over the second apron. Denver still has Peyton Watson's status unresolved, as the forward remains a restricted free agent. Oklahoma City will remain under the second apron by $6.9 million. The Thunder will also retain the use of the full Taxpayer MLE, which is valued at nearly $6.1 million.

samples.originalTitle: Draymond Green Expected To Re-Sign With Warriors For $28M
samples.originalSummary: With their pursuit of LeBron James having come up short, the Golden State Warriors are expected to pivot to re-signing Draymond Green. The expectation is the Green will re-sign at a figure close to the $28 million player option that he opted out of at the beginning of the offseason. Green has always been expected to stay with Golden State. The question was what kind of contract the veteran forward would re-sign for. The Warriors had been keeping flexibility, in case James chose to sign with them. Now that James has picked the Philadelphia 76ers, Mike Dunleavy Jr. can turn to re-signing Green, De'Anthony Melton and filling out the rest of his roster.

samples.originalTitle: Stephen Curry On LeBron James' Decision: 'You Don't Envision Anything Until It Happens'
samples.originalSummary: Stephen Curry addressed LeBron James' decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers rather than the Golden State Warriors, speaking Saturday from Moses Moody's youth camp. "That's why you don't envision anything until it happens," said Curry. "There's a lot of moving parts." Curry had hoped James would choose Golden State, believing the Warriors had a legitimate chance to land him. Once the decision went the other way, he quickly returned to the reality the team has faced for much of the past four seasons where they have been beyond the circle of realistic title contenders. Curry pointed to the injuries suffered by Jimmy Butler and Moody as the real factor shaping the Warriors' outlook, regardless of what happened with James. "The through line," said Curry, "which is hard on anybody in this situation, especially with us keeping this thing together, is knowing that when Jimmy got hurt and Moses got hurt, the whole calculus of everything changes. How do you get through their absence and still stay at a certain level? And then how that goes into this year. It's the same deal. So, I'm a realist on that." Curry acknowledged the front office explored various options to build the best possible roster around him, but said those injuries ultimately reshaped what was realistic heading into the season. "Sure," said Curry, "I'm hopeful for all the creative ideas of getting the best team possible. We had those conversations. But when you have injuries at the top like that, it's always gonna change."

samples.originalTitle: Warriors Focused On Building Team For After Stephen Curry Retires
samples.originalSummary: The Golden State Warriors were hopeful of signing LeBron James this summer. The team even looked at trading for Anthony Davis, as a means to entice James to sign in the Bay Area. However, these are short-term moves for Golden State. The Warriors real focus is reportedly on building a roster for after Stephen Curry retires. "What (team governor Joe) Lacob wants to do, and this might get Warriors fans mad. He wants to build the next team after Steph Curry," veteran reporter Tim Kawakami said on a recent episode of the TK Show . "I don't know how possible that is, but Lacob has a very keen interest in... this organization's going to show what it can do with Steph Curry and then after Steph Curry." This isn't to suggest that the Warriors are punting on the remainder of Curry's career. Instead, Golden State seems to be looking at short-term moves to build around their aging superstar, while keeping flexibility open for the post-Curry years.
